solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rapid pace cut short — a blow!

blocks.note: first sense: a brisk speed, as in moving at a good rate; also, to cut short is to trim
second sense: a sharp smack, as in a cuff round the ear

explanation.walkthrough: Really three meanings in a row: a rapid pace, to cut short, and a blow. The dash makes it read like a breathless report of an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers a brisk speed, the act of trimming something, and a quick sharp smack with the hand.

clue.text: Ancient Med city gate, arch, recollected

indicators.note: read as re-collected, gathered up again into a different arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An archaeologist remembers the gate and arch of some ancient Mediterranean city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recollected' seems to mean remembered, but split as re-collected it means the letters are gathered again in a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Carthage was the great Phoenician trading port on the North African coast, destroyed by Rome in 146 BC.

clue.text: Enticing learner — University indication of engagement?

blocks.note: L is the learner plate on a British car
standard abbreviation for university
an engagement ring signals a couple are betrothed

explanation.surface: A student at university showing off a ring that hints at a wedding to come.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'indication of engagement' is a playful way of describing a piece of jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Luring means tempting or drawing someone in, often with a bait or promise of reward.

clue.text: City celebrity interrupted by steel band at first

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of each of the two words before it
something interrupted has other material break into its middle

blocks.note: a lion is a much-feted famous person, as in a literary lion
the opening letters of steel and band

explanation.surface: A famous musician's performance is disrupted by a Caribbean steel band.
explanation.walkthrough: A steel band is a Caribbean ensemble playing tuned oil drums; here only its initials matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisbon is the capital of Portugal, sitting on the estuary of the Tagus river.

clue.text: One with income from property, not so much? Otherwise!

blocks.note: a smaller amount
or, as in do it or else

explanation.surface: A landlord asks whether rental earnings are falling, then insists they are not.
explanation.definitionFit: A lessor grants a lease and receives rent from the tenant, so earns money from owning a building or land.

clue.text: Nautical equipment transaction reported

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by voice, so the sound is what counts

blocks.note: a sale is a commercial deal

explanation.surface: News of a deal for some boating gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A sail is the canvas sheet rigged on a mast to catch the wind and drive a vessel.

clue.text: Perhaps catch by chance located in this country it’s said

indicators.note: what is said is heard rather than read, so the sound matters

blocks.note: where we are, as opposed to over there

explanation.surface: Someone wonders if a fugitive might be caught by luck, being somewhere in this country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch' suggests arresting someone, but it means hearing; 'perhaps' marks the definition as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch something by chance can mean hearing words not meant for you, which is exactly eavesdropping accidentally.

clue.text: Happy experience parking by field? Quite

blocks.note: P is the road sign for a car park
lea is a poetic word for a meadow
as an emphatic reply, quite and sure both mean certainly

explanation.surface: Someone asked whether parking in a field was a joy replies 'Quite!'
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasure is enjoyment or delight, and a pleasure can be an enjoyable event or occasion.

clue.text: One aims to shoot bird by river

blocks.note: a long-billed wading bird
standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A hunter takes aim at a bird beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The snipe is hard to shoot, which is where the word for a hidden marksman came from.
explanation.definitionFit: A sniper is a marksman who fires from a concealed position, someone whose job is taking aim.

clue.text: To higher level as purist possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements the letters might take

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A purist might aim for loftier standards.
explanation.definitionFit: Going upstairs means climbing to the floor above, so moving towards a higher storey.

clue.text: Plan is doomed from the start, dead, outsiders leave

indicators.note: from the start takes only the opening letter of each word before it
when outsiders leave, only the inner letters of the word remain

blocks.note: opening letters of is and doomed
the word with its first and last letters gone

explanation.surface: A gloomy verdict: the scheme was doomed from the outset and is now dead.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a thought or scheme for doing something, much like a proposal or plan.

clue.text: This is potentially dangerous, it may end disastrously

indicators.note: something gone disastrously has been wrecked and its parts scattered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning label: this stuff is risky and things could finish badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a description of the answer, with the fodder hidden in a natural phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynamite is a high explosive, about as hazardous a substance as you can handle.

clue.text: Worker’s greed ran wild

indicators.note: running wild means behaving without order, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An employee's greed got out of control.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardener is someone employed to tend plants and grounds, one example of a labourer.

clue.text: Bustling activity in sandbox on regular basis

indicators.note: regular means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Children busily playing in a sandpit day after day.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado is fuss and commotion, as in much ado about nothing.

clue.text: Those inside sect with figure in charge, joyful

indicators.note: those inside are the letters within the word, leaving its outer ones behind

blocks.note: the two inner letters
a stat is a statistic, a number
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: Members of a religious sect are overjoyed to have a leader in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstatic means overwhelmed with delight, a far stronger synonym for happy or joyful.

clue.text: Winter coming is too much for contact system

indicators.note: the answer is held within more than enough letters, so the phrase holds it inside

blocks.note: drop the W and the final ING

explanation.surface: The approaching winter will overwhelm the communications network.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is longer than one word of the fodder, so it spans the gap between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An intercom is a two-way speaker system for talking between rooms or buildings.

clue.text: Awkward position as public official misses centrepiece

indicators.note: missing the centrepiece means the single letter in the very middle is dropped

blocks.note: an official who investigates sudden deaths

explanation.surface: An official in an awkward spot has lost the central piece of a display.
explanation.walkthrough: CORONER has seven letters, so its centre is the fourth, the second O.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a corner, as in painted into a corner, is an idiom for a tricky predicament.

clue.text: New OC aims to produce colourful design?

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so the letters are formed into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written; OC is an officer commanding
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newly arrived commanding officer sets goals to come up with a bright scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is only an example: a picture from coloured tiles.
explanation.definitionFit: A mosaic is a picture or pattern built from many small pieces of coloured stone or glass.

clue.text: Dress artist’s recalled, reaching India

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters run back the other way

blocks.note: RA, a Royal Academician, plus the 's
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An artist remembers a frock, on arriving in India.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A sari is a long length of cloth wrapped as a garment, worn by women in South Asia.

clue.text: Heavy defeat — manager finally dismissed

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

blocks.note: the word's last letter
a batsman dismissed in cricket is out

explanation.surface: After a thrashing on the pitch, the manager is at last sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: A rout is a crushing victory in which the losing side is completely overwhelmed.

clue.text: Investigation about burn, achy when uncovered

indicators.note: uncovered means stripped of its covering, the outer letters

blocks.note: re means concerning
to scorch
the inner two letters

explanation.surface: A medical inquiry into a burn that aches once its dressing is off.
explanation.definitionFit: Research is systematic study to discover facts, which is a kind of inquiry or probe.

clue.text: Name caught by everyone

blocks.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
everyone is all; by joins the pieces

explanation.surface: A name everyone heard.
explanation.definitionFit: To call someone something is to give them a title, as in they call him Bob.

clue.text: Deny any connection with noise, as animal’s inside

indicators.note: inside places one thing within the other, splitting its letters

blocks.note: a loud racket
a female pig; the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: Someone denies responsibility for a racket coming from an animal shut indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s on the animal is read as 'is', so the animal is inside the noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown someone is to refuse to acknowledge them, cutting all ties publicly.

clue.text: Entitled to compete and fit for match?

blocks.note: first meaning: qualified to take part
second meaning: desirable as a marriage partner

explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' reads as a sporting fixture after 'compete', but here it is a marriage match.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means meeting the rules for entry, and describes a single person regarded as a good catch.

clue.text: One owing money returning bed to seller in the end

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read from right to left
in the end takes only the closing letter of the word before

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the word's last letter

explanation.surface: Someone in debt sends a bed back to the shop that sold it.
explanation.definitionFit: A debtor is a person who has borrowed and still has a sum to repay.
